_doc: Bounties posted on bounty boards (BOUNTY-001). Top level: hunt_chance (0..1, chance per exploring day in the bounty's region that the hunted foe's trail turns up; default 0.3), max_active (hunts at once; only 1 is supported, default 1), offers (how many bounties a board lists to one character, default 3; a board lists hunts in its own region first, then neighbouring regions, then the rest). bounties: [{id, enemy (an id in enemies.json), region (an id in regions.json), min_realm / max_realm (optional realm ids; max_realm absent = no cap), min_stage (optional int >= 0, needs min_realm; same meaning as the encounters' min_stage), reward_stones (int > 0, paid on a win), days (int >= 7, how long the hunt stays open once taken), cooldown_days (int >= 0, before the same bounty can be taken again after it is claimed, lapses or is abandoned), text (non-empty, the posting)}]. The active hunt lives in CharacterData.bounty {id, until_day}; cooldowns in CharacterData.bounty_cooldowns.

bounties.text: Qingshi farmers pay 40 stones for the iron-bristled boar that keeps wrecking their fences.
Marsh-edge herb gatherers offer 120 stones for the blood-eyed wolf that has taken three of their own.
The ridge miners' guild posts 400 stones for the head of the black iron bear king that closed their richest vein.
Qingshi stallholders pool 30 stones to see the drunk outer disciple who shakes them down for wine money sent home with a sore head.
The Qingshi elders offer 100 stones to whoever ends the roadside rogue who robs travellers at the village gate.
Misty Forest woodcutters pool 110 stones for the stone-hide boar king that has driven them from the old groves.
The Fallen Star market wardens pay 45 stones for the rogue cultivator who preys on stallholders after dark.
A Pavilion factor posts 130 stones for the sword madman who cuts down every caravan guard he meets on the road.
Azure Cloud outer disciples offer 50 stones for the crane that steals spirit grain from the cliff terraces.
The Azure Cloud Sword Pavilion posts 420 stones for the thunderwing roc that rakes the cliff-side halls.
Marsh boatmen offer 130 stones to lay the drowned yin ghost that drags skiffs under at midnight.
The ridge miners' guild pays 140 stones for the iron-horn rhino that tramples their ore carts.
